winning_case.argument: Allen, because the best quarterback is the one who's on the field every week.

royce.claim: Take Allen, because he has answered the question in January and is carrying the Bills now.
supports: Playoff record as a starter, 8-7 over 15 starts against Lamar's 3-5 over 8 (F22, F23)
Team result and the player's own production this season: 6-1 as a starter and 9 rushing touchdowns against Lamar's 1 (F29, F34, F35)
The read of how Allen plays: a runner who also throws it deep, tied to his rushing yards (F17)
royce.answer: Concedes Lamar's two MVPs and 79-33 record, then argues the question is who you want in January and right now, and the playoff record answers it (F10, F21).

deacon.claim: Take Lamar, because when he plays he leads every efficiency number this season.
supports: EPA per dropback and success rate, both first among qualifying quarterbacks (F20, F32)
Honors voted on over years: 2 MVPs and 3 first-team All-Pros (F10, F11)
Turning Allen's interceptions: 5 against Lamar's 1 (F24, F25)
deacon.answer: Concedes Lamar's 112 dropbacks are fewer and last season's EPA was ordinary, and says his résumé shows what a healthy Lamar is. Ends by conceding he can't take a quarterback who is on injured reserve (F27, F4).

lonnie.claim: Take Allen, because he's on the field every week and gives the Bills a runner and a passer in one.
supports: Availability: Allen has played every game in 5 of his last 5 full seasons, while Lamar missed a quarter or more in 2 and is on injured reserve today (F3, F6, F4)
Efficiency on the bigger body of work: Allen's EPA ranks second on 241 dropbacks, and last season he ranked 8th to Lamar's 18th (F19, F26, F27)
Role: Allen's running is part of the offense, with 270 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns (F17, F34)
lonnie.answer: Concedes Lamar leads this season's rate stats and says a rate stat is worth something only when the player is on the field. Names what would flip him: a healthy Lamar holding that EPA over a longer run.

beats: Opening positions: Lonnie says Allen on availability, Deacon says Lamar on this season's rates, and Lonnie answers with the dropback counts.
Main clash: Royce's picture of Allen and the 6-1 record against Deacon's interceptions turn, and Royce answers with the rushing touchdowns.
Exposed weakness: Lonnie's last-season question puts Deacon's case on a one-season rate that is up from 2025, and Royce brings the playoff record.
Decisive exchange: Lonnie asks who plays Sunday, and Deacon has to concede that his case only works if Lamar is on the field.
